subject: Dedicated reservation options — cluster sizing & staggered onboarding for Elmwood AI
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena@elmwood.ai>, Samir Qureshi <samirq@elmwood.ai>
Cc: camila.reyes@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated reservation options — draft proposal attached

Hi Elena / Samir,

Thanks again for the time last week. Based on the usage profile you shared (peak inference bursts for batch scoring during business hours, and steady low-latency interactive traffic overnight), we put together three dedicated reservation options that balance predictability and cost. See the attached PDF for slides and the CSV for the baseline sizing workbook. High level: 

- Option A — Conservative floor: 24min GPUs (2x12), small burst pool. Good if you want spend predictability and lower monthly commitment.
- Option B — Balanced ramp: 48min GPUs with staged activation (24 -> 36 -> 48 over 90 days). Best for throughput growth while keeping initial cash outlay moderate.
- Option C — Aggressive throughput: 96min GPUs with immediate burst lanes and pre-warmed instances for low tail latency.

Key trade-offs called out in the doc: model parallelism limits depending on your chosen model (we assumed 70B quantized), KV cache warm-up costs, and expected token-hour consumption for the batch scoring job. We included a recommended ramp schedule for Option B (milestones and activation triggers) because that tends to be the pragmatic path for teams that want to validate early while preserving the option to scale.

Next steps I propose: pick 1 option as the basis, we iterate the ramp triggers and finalize the minimum GPU floor for the order form. If you want, Camila can join the technical call to validate the warm-start and cache strategies before commit.

Attachments: elmwood_dedicated_options_v3.pdf, cluster-sizing-sheet.csv

Regards,

Jonas Weber

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options — draft proposal attached (internal)

Jonas / Dev — quick notes to prepare for the Elmwood call: 

- Minimum for sub-150ms P95: for their stated model and token-length distribution, we should target a warmed baseline of ~30 effective GPUs (we recommend mapping to 2xA100-80 configurations) — that accounts for KV cache hit-rate ~65% and interactive tail. That maps closest to Option A+ (a slight uplift to A).
- Option B ramp: propose concrete milestones: Day 0 -> 24 GPUs, Day 30 -> +12 (36), Day 60 -> +12 (48). Activation triggers: sustained 7-day rolling average >70% utilization or a signed PO for expanded capacity.
- Warm-start credits: month 1 crediting can offset up to 50% of pre-warm costs if customer agrees to a 3-month staged activation clause; otherwise they pay full for active GPUs. We should be explicit about the credit amortization schedule in the SOW (CSV has amort table).
- Burst lanes: typically 1–2 week lead time if within existing capacity; cost = hourly burst rate * hours used + small activation fee. If they want guaranteed burst we need a short-term reserve which comes with a minimum 2-week commit.

Action items for call: Dev to prepare expected P95 curves for 24/36/48/96 GPU baselines; Jonas to present commercial options and the credit amortization language; I'll take notes and confirm the ramp wording for the SOW.

Camila Reyes
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Elena / Samir — thanks for the questions and for the call today. Quick summary and proposed path forward so finance can review: 

Agreed baseline: Option B (Balanced ramp) with the following adjustments we discussed: 
- Commit to an initial floor of 24 GPUs active Day 0.
- Automatic uplift triggers: Day 30 -> +12 GPUs (36) if 7-day avg utilization >70% OR earlier if Elmwood signs an expansion PO.
- Final state Day 90 -> 48 GPUs.
- We will include a warm-start credit schedule in the SOW: 50% offset on pre-warm costs amortized over 3 months (see attached amortization table in cluster-sizing-sheet.csv).

Burst / campaign guidance: we can provide 2-week guaranteed burst lanes with a 2-week minimum commit. Lead time is typically 5 business days if capacity is available; longer if we need to provision new hardware. Estimated incremental cost shown in the attached PDF (section 3).

Next steps: 
1) I will upload a draft SOW with the ramp triggers and credit wording (DocuSign link below). Please review and indicate scope changes by EOD Nov 29.
2) Once SOW is agreed, Elmwood finance will sign the order form and we schedule activation.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/elmwood/ELM-2026-03
